what_its_for: Colesevelam is used to lower bad cholesterol (LDL) in your blood. It is also used along with diet and exercise to help control blood sugar levels in adults with type 2 diabetes. Lower cholesterol helps reduce your risk of heart attack and stroke.
how_to_take: Take colesevelam exactly as your doctor tells you. Tablets: Swallow the tablets whole with a full glass of water (8 ounces). Take with meals. Do not crush, chew, or cut the tablets. Powder packets: Mix the entire packet into 4 to 8 ounces of water, fruit juice, or diet soft drinks. Stir well and drink right away. Never take the powder dry. Always take this medicine with food and plenty of liquids to help it work properly and to avoid stomach upset.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 3 tablets twice a day with meals, or 6 tablets once a day with a meal. If using the powder, the usual dose is one 3.75 gram packet once a day or one 1.875 gram packet twice a day with meals. Your doctor may adjust your dose based on your condition. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember with a meal and plenty of water. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store colesevelam tablets and powder packets at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the medicine away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Colesevelam can interfere with how your body absorbs other medicines. Take any other medications at least 4 hours before or 4 hours after taking colesevelam. This is especially important for thyroid medicine (like levothyroxine), birth control pills, cyclosporine, glipizide, glyburide, and fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, and K). Talk to your pharmacist about all your other medicines. Avoid taking this medicine without food or without enough liquid, as this may cause choking or stomach problems.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you have: severe stomach pain, constipation that does not go away or is very uncomfortable, trouble swallowing, nausea or vomiting that is severe, signs of very high triglycerides (a type of fat in the blood) such as severe stomach pain, or signs of low blood sugar (shakiness, dizziness, sweating, confusion) if you are also taking diabetes medicines. Also call your doctor if you notice your other medicines do not seem to be working as well as usual.
when_it_works: Colesevelam starts working right away, but you may not feel any different because high cholesterol and high blood sugar usually have no symptoms. Your doctor will check your cholesterol or blood sugar levels after a few weeks to see how well the medicine is working. It is important to keep taking it even if you feel fine. Continue eating a healthy diet and exercising as directed by your doctor.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Colesevelam is generally considered safe during pregnancy, but it may reduce the absorption of important vitamins. Talk to your doctor before using if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. Children: Colesevelam tablets can be used in children aged 10 to 17 years who have a genetic condition causing high cholesterol. Powder packets are approved for children aged 10 and older. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have any kidney or liver problems before starting this medicine. People with a history of bowel blockage, swallowing problems, or very high triglycerides should not use colesevelam without talking to their doctor first.
